answer: A farm that wants 132 keys therefore pays 132 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the whisper seed, the timber timing is verifiable from the ferrous record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 485 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
